title: Q2 Fast-Correlation Attack Beyond Grover Search
summary: Attempts on eight stream ciphers have not beaten Grover search; finding a Q2 fast-correlation attack that recovers an initial state or key faster remains open.

formal_statement.body: Find a $\mathrm{Q2}$ fast-correlation attack on at least one of Grain v1, Grain-128, Grain-128a, Fruit-v2, Fruit-80, Plantlet, SNOW-V, or SNOW-Vi that recovers the initial state or secret key faster than exhaustive key search with Grover's algorithm. Attempts to quantum-speed classical fast-correlation attacks on these targets have not produced such an attack. For every target except SNOW-V and SNOW-Vi, the identified obstacle is that the absolute correlations are too small. SNOW-V and SNOW-Vi instead use $512$-bit LFSRs and $256$-bit keys and have absolute correlations greater than $2^{-50}$, but the QFCA2 quantum fast-correlation method still has time complexity at least $2^{150}$ because of its $2^{18}\ell^4$ factor when $\ell=512$.

scope.domain: Quantum fast-correlation cryptanalysis of LFSR-based stream ciphers.
assumptions: The attack is evaluated in the Q2 model.
parameters: Target cipher: one of Grain v1, Grain-128, Grain-128a, Fruit-v2, Fruit-80, Plantlet, SNOW-V, or SNOW-Vi
Recovery target: the initial state or secret key
Performance benchmark: exhaustive key search with Grover's algorithm
Absolute correlation: the identified bottleneck for every target except SNOW-V and SNOW-Vi
LFSR length ell: equal to 512 for SNOW-V and SNOW-Vi and used in the stated QFCA2 time factor
Key size: 256 bits for SNOW-V and SNOW-Vi
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a Q2 fast-correlation attack on at least one named cipher that recovers the initial state or secret key faster than Grover exhaustive key search.

citations.label: Quantum Algorithms for Fast Correlation Attacks on LFSR-Based Stream Ciphers

progress.summary: The source reports that attempts to speed up classical fast-correlation attacks on all eight ciphers produced no Q2 attack faster than Grover exhaustive search. It attributes the obstacle to small correlations except for SNOW-V and SNOW-Vi, where QFCA2 still has time complexity at least 2^150.
citation_labels: Akinori Hosoyamada et al., Quantum Algorithms for Fast Correlation Attacks on LFSR-Based Stream Ciphers
